# Rich Visualization Library repository guidance

- The product name is **Rich Visualization Library** and its short brand is **Rich Viz**. `RichViz` remains a technical API/package identifier. “Rich Educational Visualization” is a legacy name that may appear in older host paths, schemas or saved content; preserve those compatibility identifiers unless a migration is explicitly in scope.
- For a first installation into a host project, use `skills/richviz-integration/SKILL.md`. For updating, migrating, comparing, or validating an already integrated copy, use `skills/richviz-updater/SKILL.md`. Each skill links to the other; do not use the installation workflow as a blind upgrade procedure.
- When installing or updating Rich Viz in any project, inspect the host and existing dependencies before editing; select only compatible source modules, adapters, assets and licensed engines needed for the requested use. Do not recreate examples or copy vendor engines outside their separately licensed directories.
- Preserve the public JSON schema and the `RichViz.render()` / `mountVisualization()` API. Changes to either require migration notes.
- Keep visual types in `src/schema/`, renderer routing in `src/RichVisualizationRegistry.js`, examples under the single root `Examples/`, and adapters in `src/adapters/`.
- External engines stay isolated under `External-Libraries/<id>/active/`, with their license and notices. Do not add a CDN requirement.
- Validate declarative input; never render article/example input as HTML or executable code.
- Keep modules lazy-loaded and scoped. Do not mount hidden examples until needed.
- Keep diagrams keyboard-accessible, responsive, RTL-aware, and paired with a text alternative.
- Run focused tests for changed modules and a browser gallery audit for renderer changes.
- Do not add assets without recording author, source, license, redistribution and commercial-use terms in `Assets/catalog.json`.
- Prevent duplicate assets: before adding an icon, illustration, sticker, image or pack, compare canonical names/IDs and SHA-256 file hashes against the existing library and staged additions. Do not add identical files under alternate names or repeated copies from another pack; keep distinct icon families in explicitly named collections with their own provenance and licenses.
- The Visual Browser is a live visual index of the library, not a separately authored examples collection. It must derive cards, previews, counts, categories, filters and stable references from the canonical example/type/icon registries and discovered/catalogued assets. Whenever library examples, types, icons, SVGs, images or stickers are added, removed or renamed, the browser must reflect that change automatically; do not maintain a second manual inventory. Preserve the library content and validate that each discoverable item appears in the browser after changes to its presentation.
- Any Rich Viz software, schema, renderer, adapter, registry, documentation or asset update must update the Visual Browser in the same change so that every supported/current item and capability remains browsable with accurate counts, categories and references; include focused synchronization tests.
- Every Visual Browser page must use the shared header, navigation, theme control, version badge, footer and responsive design system. Icons, standalone SVG illustrations, stickers, the project overview, and About are independent pages with separate routes; never merge these content categories or present one category's files as another. Empty categories remain discoverable and explain that no items are currently registered.
- Keep the browser's two-level information architecture: primary pages are Home, Explore Library, Project and About; Explore Library is a dashboard whose secondary navigation leads to Diagrams, Icons, Application Icons, SVG and Stickers. New library content must flow into its existing category page and registry-derived counts without adding duplicate manually maintained inventory. Keep the five collection pages on stable routes and preserve cross-page search state in URLs.
- The repository root `VERSION` is the canonical product release version. Keep the `package.json` version, README version badge and active source asset-cache `?v=` references consistent with it. Run `npm run validate:version` (also included in `npm test`) before a release. Do not rewrite historical changelog versions, third-party library versions or independently versioned skills.
- Original RichViz material is licensed under Apache-2.0. Third-party components retain their original licenses and notices; review `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and bundled vendor notice files before changing distribution.


Before troubleshooting visualization controls, layout, connectors or interaction, read `docs/RICH-VIZ-PROBLEMS-AND-SOLUTIONS.md` and `docs/READER-CONTROLS.md`. Every icon-only button requires a clear localized tooltip and accessible label. Update reusable guards when fixing a new cause.
